prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” HVAC company for every situation — the right choice depends on your location in Greater Houston, the type/brand and age of your AC, whether it’s an emergency, and your budget. I can help pick the best option for your situation, but first:

Quick questions
- What zip code or neighborhood are you in?
- Is this an emergency (no cooling now) or a routine repair/maintenance?
- Do you know the AC brand and approximate age?
- Any preference for price vs. warranty vs. fast response?

Well-reviewed Houston companies to consider
(These are commonly recommended, well-established local options — you should still vet them for your specific needs.)
- John Moore Services — long-established, offers 24/7 emergency service and maintenance plans.  
- AirPro Houston — local company, handles residential and commercial, offers financing options.  
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (Houston franchise) — national chain with local technicians, available for emergency repairs and installs.  
- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning (local franchise) — offers prompt service windows and guaranteed response times.  
- ABC Home & Commercial Services — full-service HVAC, maintenance agreements and warranties.

How to choose and vet any company
- Check licensing: verify the contractor’s license with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR).  
- Certifications: look for NATE-certified technicians.  
- Insurance: confirm liability insurance and worker’s comp.  
- Reviews & complaints: read Google/Yelp/Angi and BBB ratings, but weigh recent reviews most heavily.  
- Get multiple quotes: get 2–3 written estimates to compare parts, labor, and warranty.  
- Ask about guarantees: ask about labor/parts warranty and whether diagnostic fees are waived if you proceed with the repair.  
- Ask details: request a written scope (what was diagnosed, what parts will be replaced, efficiency gains), and avoid high‑pressure “replace everything” pitches unless clearly necessary.  
- Emergency availability and response time: if you need immediate help, confirm arrival windows and after-hours rates.

If you tell me your zip code and whether it’s urgent (and a short description of the problem), I’ll suggest 2–3 highly relevant providers in your area and what to ask them on the phone.
